function.name: generate_image_tool
function.description: Generates an image based on the provided description and saves it with the specified file name. The image description should be detailed to ensure the resulting image matches the desired subject and surroundings; otherwise, these aspects will be chosen randomly. This function is not intended for generating images from textual data. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

desc.description: A single string that provides a detailed description of the desired image. For example, 'a sunset over the mountains with a lake in the foreground'.

file_name.description: The name of the file to which the generated image will be saved. It should include the file extension, such as 'image.png'.

function.name: tts_tool
function.description: Converts the provided text content to speech and saves the resulting audio to a file. This function is intended for voice narration and should be used accordingly. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The text content that needs to be converted to speech.

speaker.description: The voice to be used for the text-to-speech conversion.

file_name.description: The name of the file to save the audio output without the extension. If left empty, a default name will be generated based on the content.

function.name: write_markdown_tool
function.description: Writes the provided content to a Markdown (.md) file on the disk. This function should be used when there is a need to persist text data in Markdown format as a result of a user action or a process that requires saving information in a structured text file. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The Markdown formatted text content to be written to the file.

filename.description: The name of the file to which the Markdown content will be written. If not provided, a default filename will be used.

function.name: write_html_tool
function.description: Writes an HTML file to disk with the given content. Ensures HTML tags within the content are properly closed. This function should be used when there is a need to save HTML content to a file as part of a 'save' operation. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The HTML content to be written to the file. Must contain valid HTML structure.

filename.description: The name of the file to which the HTML content will be written. If not provided, a default filename will be used.

function.name: search_web_tool
function.description: Executes a search query using the DuckDuckGo search engine and returns a specified number of search results from a given source. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

query.description: The search term or phrase to be queried.

num_results.description: The maximum number of search results to return. A positive integer.

source.description: The source from which the search results should be fetched.

function.name: get_url_content
function.description: Scrapes the specified URL for textual data and returns the content as a string. This function is useful for extracting information from web pages when a URL is provided. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The web address of the page to scrape. It should be a valid URL format, such as 'http://www.example.com'.

timeout.description: The maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, with a default value that allows for a reasonable amount of time for most web pages to load.

user_agent.description: The User-Agent string to be used for the HTTP request to simulate a particular browser, which is optional. Some websites may require this for access.

Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑run example** that shows how to create a Google Cloud Compute Engine instance with an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU and Ubuntu 20.04 LTS using the **REST API**. I’ve broken it down into three parts: 1. **Prerequisites & setup** – what you need to do before you can call the API. 2. **The HTTP request** – the exact `curl` command (or equivalent) you can run. 3. **Optional gcloud wrapper** – a one‑liner that does the same thing via the `gcloud` CLI. --- ## 1. Prerequisites & Setup | Step | What to do | Why | |------|------------|-----| | **Enable Compute Engine API** | In the Cloud Console → APIs & Services → Library → Search “Compute Engine” → Enable. | Needed for all Compute Engine calls. | | **Create a project** | Cloud Console → IAM & Admin → Create a new project. | Keeps resources isolated. | | **Set up billing** | Cloud Console → Billing → Link a billing account to your project. | Compute Engine requires billing. | | **Create a service account** | Cloud Console → IAM & Admin → Service Accounts → Create → Grant “Editor” (or more restrictive) role. | Needed for programmatic access. | | **Generate a key** | In the service account → Keys → Add Key → JSON. | Gives you a file you’ll use for authentication. | | **Install `gcloud`** | `curl https://sdk.cloud.google.com | bash` → restart shell. | Optional but handy for debugging. | | **Authenticate** | `gcloud auth activate-service-account --key-file=path/to/key.json` | Sets the default credentials for `gcloud` and `curl`. | | **Set default project & zone** | `gcloud config set project YOUR_PROJECT_ID`
`gcloud config set compute/zone YOUR_ZONE` | Makes subsequent commands simpler. | | **Check GPU quota** | `gcloud compute accelerator-types list --filter="zone:YOUR_ZONE"`
`gcloud compute accelerator-types describe nvidia-tesla-a6000 --zone=YOUR_ZONE` | Ensure you have quota for A6000 GPUs. | > **Tip:** If you’re new to quotas, you can request an increase from the Cloud Console → Quotas page. --- ## 2. The HTTP Request (REST API) Below is a `curl` command that will create the instance. Replace the placeholder values (`YOUR_PROJECT_ID`, `YOUR_ZONE`, etc.) with your actual values. ```bash # 1️⃣ Set variables PROJECT_ID="YOUR_PROJECT_ID" ZONE="YOUR_ZONE" # e.g., us-central1-a INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu" MACHINE_TYPE="n1-standard-8" # 8 vCPU, 30 GB RAM (adjust as needed) GPU_COUNT=1 GPU_TYPE="nvidia-tesla-a6000" DISK_SIZE_GB=100 DISK_TYPE="pd-ssd" NETWORK="default" SUBNET="default" IMAGE_FAMILY="ubuntu-2004-focal" IMAGE_PROJECT="ubuntu-os-cloud" # 2️⃣ Build the JSON payload read -r -d '' INSTANCE_JSON < **Note:** > * The `acceleratorType` field uses the **full resource name** (`zones/.../acceleratorTypes/...`). > * The `sourceImage` field pulls the latest Ubuntu 20.04 image from the official Ubuntu Cloud image project. > * If you need a different machine type or GPU count, adjust `MACHINE_TYPE`, `GPU_COUNT`, and `GPU_TYPE` accordingly. --- ## 3. Optional gcloud Wrapper If you prefer to use the `gcloud` CLI (which handles authentication, formatting, and error handling for you), the same instance can be created with a single command: ```bash gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE_NAME" \ --project="$PROJECT_ID" \ --zone="$ZONE" \ --machine-type="$MACHINE_TYPE" \ --accelerator="type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=$GPU_COUNT" \ --image-family="$IMAGE_FAMILY" \ --image-project="$IMAGE_PROJECT" \ --boot-disk-size="$DISK_SIZE_GB"GB \ --boot-disk-type="$DISK_TYPE" \ --boot-disk-device-name="$INSTANCE_NAME" \ --tags=http-server,https-server \ --metadata=enable-oslogin=TRUE ``` > **Why use `gcloud`?** > * It automatically selects the correct GPU driver installation script. > * It provides helpful progress output and error messages. > * It’s easier to read and maintain for most users. --- ## 4. Verify the Instance After the API call completes, you can verify that the instance is running: ```bash gcloud compute instances list --filter="name=$INSTANCE_NAME" --format="table(name,zone,status,gpuAccelerators)" ``` You should see something like: ``` NAME ZONE STATUS GPU ACCELERATORS rtx-a6000-ubuntu us-central1-a RUNNING nvidia-tesla-a6000:1 ``` --- ## 5. SSH Into the Instance Once the instance is `RUNNING`, you can SSH into it: ```bash gcloud compute ssh "$INSTANCE_NAME" --zone="$ZONE" ``` Inside the VM, you can confirm the GPU is visible: ```bash nvidia-smi ``` You should see the RTX A6000 listed with its driver version. --- ## 6. Clean Up When you’re done, delete the instance to avoid ongoing charges: ```bash gcloud compute instances delete "$INSTANCE_NAME" --zone="$ZONE" --quiet ``` --- ## Recap - **Prerequisites**: Enable API, set up billing, create service account, install `gcloud`. - **REST API**: `curl` command with a JSON payload that includes the GPU accelerator. - **gcloud CLI**: One‑liner that does the same thing. - **Verification**: Check status, SSH, run `nvidia-smi`. - **Cleanup**: Delete the instance when finished. Feel free to copy/paste the snippets into your terminal, adjust the variables, and run! If you hit any errors, let me know the exact error message and I’ll help troubleshoot.
